dedupe_keys.name: china digital twin of a large new hospital built through continuous lifecycle integration

description: This case study reports a digital twin built for a large newly constructed hospital in China. The authors, from Shanghai Construction Group, argue that building information models alone cannot keep up with the real-time status and data volume of hospital facility systems, medical equipment, security and business systems. Their continuous lifecycle integration method, with the general contractor involved early, integrated static and dynamic data from more than 20 management systems across design, construction, pre-operation and operation. A digital twin software system with real-time visual management and artificial intelligence diagnosis modules was developed and deployed in a new control centre, from which managers can see the status of the whole hospital and receive facility diagnoses and operating suggestions. The article was published in 2020 in Advances in Civil Engineering and is free to read online under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Coverage is one hospital, not named in the abstract. Caveats: benefits are reported qualitatively by the builder, and the software is proprietary. The authors report that the system had been running steadily for over a year, reducing energy use, avoiding facility faults, cutting repair requests and improving routine maintenance. Simulation uses: an example architecture for hospital facility digital twins used in operations and resilience management. Related records: the Yongin Severance virtual hospital for IT outage training (case_study-yongin-severance-hospital-it-outage-digital-twin-training) is another hospital digital twin.
